text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
CORN SALE - Exporters reported the sale of 162,000 tonnes of U.S. corn for delivery to unknown destinations during 1997/98, U.S. Agriculture Department said Friday.

- A group of South Korean feed milling companies, known as the Big Feed Mills, bought 52,500 tonnes of corn from Japanese trading house Mitsui & Company Ltd, traders said. Arrival was set by September 30 to Inchon and Kunsan, they said.
WHEAT SALE - Egypt added 116,500 tonnes to its purchases of U.S. wheat in the week ending May 22, the Agriculture Department said on Friday.
CORN TENDER - The Philippine Association of Feed Millers Inc sought tenders on Thursday for 50,000 tonnes yellow corn, an official of the group told Reuters.

CORN TENDERS - Naseem Agriculture of Abu Dhabi is seeking a consignment of 10,000 or 15,000 tonnes of U.S., Argentine or South African yellow maize for shipment in the second half of August, South Africa's shippers association said. Bids were invited C and F Abu Dhabi port by June 6.
- CCC said it will offer 8.2 million bushels of corn for sale from its feed grain catalog, with offers due June 3 and results announced June 4.
WHEAT TENDERS - South Korea's National Livestock Cooperatives Federation said Friday it passed on a tender to buy 52,000 tonnes of corn due to high offer prices.
- Sri Lanka seeks 50,000 to 60,000 tonnes of PL-480 wheat for June 30-July 19 shipment. Offers are due by 1630 GMT June 5 at the Sri Lankan embassy in Washington.
SOYMEAL TENDER - South Korea's National Livestock Cooperatives Federation said on Friday it had passed on a tender to buy 40,000 tonnes of soymeal due to high offer prices.
RICE TENDER - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foostuffs seeks offers June 4 to buy 12,000 tonnes of white rice for July with confirmation on June 12.

MARKET TALK - USDA said it was standing by its report of 562,700 tonnes of U.S. corn sold to Japan in the week ended May 22 for 1996/97 delivery but was double-checking with exporters. Talk circulated in grain markets on Friday that the corn was actually new crop sold for 1997/98 shipment.
